findings.title: `sanitizeSearchTerm` does not strip PostgREST `.` operator separators
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/search.ts:22 — MAX_SEARCH_TERM_LENGTH = 100
apps/api/src/lib/search.ts:29 — `.replace(/[,()."\\%*]/g, " ")` strips comma, parens, dot, quotes, backslash, `%` and `*`
apps/api/src/lib/search.ts:33 — term truncated to 100 chars
apps/api/src/__tests__/sanitize-search.test.ts:32-53 — regression suite asserts no `.`/`*`/`,`/`(`/`)`/quote/`%`/`\` survives (a.eq.b → 'a eq b')
apps/api/src/__tests__/sanitize-search.test.ts:55-64 — documented tradeoff (dots flattened) and 100-char cap asserted
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:20,104,116,128,140,156 — sanitized term interpolated into `.or("col.ilike.<term>")` filters
findings.impact: The filter-injection hardening gap is closed: dotted terms can no longer reshape the PostgREST `.or()` grammar, and term length is bounded.
findings.recommendation: No action required; keep the regression tests and the documented dot tradeoff.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: strip set now includes `.` and `*`, length capped at 100, regression tests cover a.eq.b / a*b / injection strings (fix from d48d2196). Residual: literal dots are intentionally unsearchable (documented in lib/search.ts:13-19).

findings.title: Admin global search exposes profile PII and never tenant-scopes the organizations query
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:38-70 — caller's approved memberships + roles resolved; `canSeeAllTenants` requires the super_admin profile flag AND a cross-tenant role key
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:84-86 — `email, phone` projection only on the all-tenants (super admin) path; others get `id, full_name, title`
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:91-99 — non-super callers are limited to approved members of their own orgs and never fall back to all (empty list → `__none__`)
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:153-163 — organizations query now `.in("id", scopedOrgIds)` unless the caller is a true platform admin
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:200-202 — the all-tenants path is recorded in the audit event (`allTenants`)
apps/api/src/__tests__/search.test.ts:173-203 — tests assert organizations scoped to ORG_A and the reduced projection for a tenant admin
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts:136-225 — fail-closed empty scope, explicit-org narrowing, audited all-tenants path
findings.impact: Tenant admins can no longer enumerate other tenants' organizations and no longer receive email/phone from admin search; the previous cross-tenant/PII exposure is closed.
findings.recommendation: No action required for the filed finding; optionally stop matching on `email` for non-super callers (see residual).
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: organizations are org-scoped and PII is gated to super_admin (fix from d48d2196, tightened by ab783ed7). Residual: `search.ts:104` still uses `email.ilike.%q%` as a predicate for non-super callers, so a tenant admin retains a boolean oracle over staff emails they cannot read; low impact, consider dropping the email branch for non-super callers.

findings.title: Raw search terms persisted in plaintext `audit_logs.metadata`
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:191 — `crypto.createHash("sha256").update(q).digest("hex").slice(0, 16)` (truncated fingerprint)
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:193-211 — audit metadata stores `queryHash`, `queryLength`, `allTenants`, `resultCounts`; the raw term is never written
apps/api/src/__tests__/search.test.ts:205-221 — test asserts `metadata` has no `query` and does not contain `customer@example.com`
apps/api/src/services/audit.ts:34-45 — key-name redaction retained; no value-level scrubbing needed for this path
apps/worker/src/tasks/retention.ts:13,131 — audit_logs purge window is 365 days (now only a hash is retained for that window)
findings.impact: Search terms (possible PII/keywords) are no longer durably stored in plaintext for a year; only a truncated hash plus length is retained.
findings.recommendation: No action required; document the fingerprint scheme and retention in the search module doc.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: raw term removed from audit metadata and regression-tested (fix from d48d2196).

findings.title: Portal search omits documents despite SDK and documentation contract
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search-portal.ts:54-59 — response is `{ tickets, projects }` only
packages/sdk/src/search.ts:11-15 — `PortalSearchResult` declares `documents`
docs/API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md:164 — claims org-scoped portal search returns 'tickets + projects + documents'
apps/web/components/portal/PortalGlobalSearch.tsx:7-10 — portal UI type expects only tickets/projects
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-portal.test.ts:60,83 — tests assert `{ tickets: [], projects: [] }` (no documents)
findings.impact: SDK consumers and docs promise a documents array the route never returns; portal users cannot search documents; the three artifacts remain unsynchronized.
findings.recommendation: Either add a visibility-respecting documents query to search-portal.ts + portal UI, or remove `documents` from the SDK type and correct API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md; add a contract test.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: portal route unchanged (tickets/projects only), SDK and inventory doc still declare documents.

findings.title: Admin search UI silently discards the documents result set
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:221 — API response includes `documents`
apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx:7-12 — `SearchResult` type has no `documents`
apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx:62-70 — `resultCount()` sums users/organizations/tickets/projects only
apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx:118-203 — dropdown renders users/organizations/tickets/projects; no documents block
grep 'documents' apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx — no matches
findings.impact: The backend computes and transmits document matches (including the new `counts.documents`) that the admin UI never renders, so the documents-in-admin-search improvement is still not delivered end-to-end.
findings.recommendation: Add `documents` to the UI type, count and render a Documents group (and surface `counts`/`limit` while there); add an E2E assertion.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: UI unchanged; it also ignores the new `counts`/`limit` response fields.

findings.title: No search pagination or result counts; hard 5-result ceiling
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:28 — `limit = Math.min(25, Math.max(1, queryInt(req.query.limit, 5)))`
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:103,115,127,139,155 — each entity query selects with `{ count: "exact" }`
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:222-231 — response gains additive `counts` (per entity) and `limit`
apps/api/src/__tests__/search.test.ts:106-127 — asserts `?limit=10` applied and counts returned
apps/api/src/routes/search-portal.ts:42,48 — portal search still hard `.limit(5)` with no counts
apps/api/src/openapi/spec.ts:976-987 — both search routes still document only the `q` parameter
apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx:47 — UI calls `search.admin(query)` without a limit and ignores counts
packages/sdk/src/search.ts:20-21 — SDK admin call sends no `limit`
findings.impact: Admin search now has a bounded page size and totals, but portal search, both UIs, the SDK and OpenAPI were not updated: users still see 5 results with no 'show more', and no offset/cursor exists.
findings.recommendation: Extend `?limit`/counts to search-portal.ts, document `limit` in OpenAPI, add an optional limit argument + counts to the SDK, and surface a 'show more' affordance; consider an offset/cursor and note that `count: 'exact'` on five parallel queries costs extra DB work at volume.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: `?limit` (default 5, hard cap 25) + per-entity exact counts implemented for the admin route (a499e03a, mainecybertech#133). Residual: portal route, UIs, SDK and OpenAPI unchanged; no offset/cursor; exact-count cost not measured.

findings.title: Search query analytics metric is dead and the analytics summary RPC is missing
evidence: apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:68-72 — `portal_search_queries_total` counter defined
apps/api/src/lib/metrics.ts:218-220 — `recordSearchQuery()` increments it
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:213 — admin search now calls `recordSearchQuery()`
apps/api/src/routes/search-portal.ts — no metric or audit call anywhere in the portal route
apps/api/src/routes/analytics.ts:84 — `supabase.rpc("get_analytics_summary")`; grep supabase/ for `get_analytics_summary` → NO MATCHES (RPC still undefined, will 500)
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:132 — still documents `portal_search_queries_total` as 'defined, not wired'
apps/api/src/__tests__/search.test.ts:99-103 — test asserts the metric is wired for admin search
findings.impact: Admin search volume is now observable, but portal search still emits nothing (no metric, no audit), the counter name says 'portal' while only admin increments it, and the admin analytics summary endpoint still calls a non-existent database function.
findings.recommendation: Call the metric (and consider a hashed-term audit) in search-portal.ts, rename or relabel the counter to cover both routes, implement or replace `get_analytics_summary` (see SEC-P2-004), and refresh docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: admin route wired to the counter (36e5f723, IR-P2-001); RPC still absent and portal route still uninstrumented/unlogged; monitoring doc still says 'not wired'.

findings.title: Prefix/wildcard mismatch: no btree on prefix columns and no full-text (`tsvector`) search
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:29-30 — prefix term `q%` for full_name/organization name/slug and `%q%` elsewhere
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:140 — documents searched on `name` and `mime_type` (no index on either column)
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:156 — organizations searched on `slug` (no index on slug)
supabase/migrations/5302102_add_performance_indexes.sql:10-16 — 7 GIN trigram indexes (profiles.full_name/email, organizations.name, tickets.title/description, projects.name/description)
grep supabase/ + apps/api/src for `tsvector` → NO MATCHES
grep supabase/migrations for an index on organizations.slug → only idx_organizations_name_trgm exists
findings.impact: At volume, slug and document-name searches scan unindexed columns, prefix columns get trigram rather than btree plans, and there is still no ranked full-text search.
findings.recommendation: Add indexes for organizations.slug and documents.name, evaluate btree indexes for the prefix-only columns, and a `to_tsvector('english', ...)` generated column + GIN for ticket/project descriptions; validate with EXPLAIN on seeded volume.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: index migration unchanged since 9c0b88c; documents.name/mime_type and organizations.slug are searched but unindexed; no tsvector anywhere.

findings.title: Typeahead calls full search endpoints without rate limiting or a dedicated autocomplete surface
evidence: apps/api/src/app.ts:125-146 — global IP limiter (300/15 min) and `rateLimitByUser` (600/15 min) apply to every route
apps/api/src/middleware/rate-limit.ts:27-40 — per-user limiter keys on a SHA-256 of the bearer token
apps/web/components/admin/AdminGlobalSearch.tsx:38-60 — 300 ms debounce then `search.admin(query)`
apps/web/components/portal/PortalGlobalSearch.tsx:36-58 — 300 ms debounce then `search.portal(query, "")`
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:165-177 — each admin keystroke issues five parallel queries, now with `count: 'exact'` on each
grep 'autocomplete|typeahead|suggest' apps/api/src — no dedicated autocomplete endpoint; no search-specific limiter or response cache on either search route
findings.impact: Platform-wide limiters bound abuse (600 requests/15 min/user), but typeahead still fans out five exact-count queries per debounced keystroke with no dedicated lightweight endpoint or search-route throttle; amplification is bounded but not optimized.
findings.recommendation: Add a dedicated single-column autocomplete endpoint or a search-specific limiter/short-TTL cache, and increase debounce/min-length for typeahead; consider dropping `count: 'exact'` for the typeahead path.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: global per-IP/per-user rate limiters exist (present since before 9c0b88c), but no search-specific limit, no caching and no dedicated autocomplete endpoint; each admin call now also computes exact counts.

findings.title: Soft-delete columns are defined but never used by queries or deletes
evidence: supabase/migrations/5302432_drop_unused_soft_delete_columns.sql:17-31 — drops `deleted_at`/`deleted_by` from tickets/projects/documents and their indexes
supabase/migrations/5302432_drop_unused_soft_delete_columns.sql:9-13 — documents the product decision: HARD DELETE, recovery via backups/PITR
grep 'deleted_at' apps/api/src → NO MATCHES (no runtime reads/writes)
supabase/migrations/5302109_soft_delete.sql — historical add of the now-dropped columns
findings.impact: The latent 'deleted data becomes searchable if soft-delete is wired later' risk is removed by deleting the inert columns; hard deletes keep deleted rows out of search.
findings.recommendation: No action required; optionally clean up the dead defensive `deleted_at` fallbacks in the web components.
findings.note: re-verified at 8d299b8d: 5302432 removes the columns (DATA-P1-003 product decision = hard delete); no API reads remain. Residual: apps/web components still probe `ticket.deleted_at` defensively (e.g. apps/web/app/(admin)/admin/tickets/[ticketId]/page.tsx:47,84) — dead code that can never be true.

findings.title: Search module documentation is stale relative to the code
evidence: docs/modules/search.md:9,14,27 — lists users/organizations/tickets/projects only and says 'read-only across all'
docs/modules/search.md:31 — 'Admin: can search across all organizations and entities' (no longer true for tenant admins)
docs/modules/search-portal.md:4 — attributes the route to `search.ts` instead of `search-portal.ts`
docs/API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md:163-164 — `/admin` auth omits `requireAdmin`; `/portal` auth wrongly lists `requireOrgAccess`; portal entity list wrongly includes documents
docs/MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md:132 — search metric still marked 'defined, not wired'
The docs do not mention documents in admin search, the PII projection rule, `?limit`/`counts`, or the hashed search audit
findings.impact: Operators and future agents reason from contracts that contradict the implementation, including the tenant-scoping and PII rules that matter for isolation.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite docs/modules/search.md and search-portal.md against the current routes; fix API_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.md and MONITORING_AND_ALERTING.md; document the `?limit`/counts shape.
findings.note: re-verified still open at 8d299b8d: all cited doc lines unchanged; drift has grown (documents, org scoping, PII gating, limit/counts, metric wiring all undocumented).

findings.title: Admin global search returns private/internal documents without applying the `can_read_document` visibility filter
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:26 — admin search always uses `getSupabaseAdmin()` (service role; RLS bypassed)
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:137-147 — documents query scoped by `organization_id` only; selects `id, name, mime_type, visibility, organization_id` with no visibility/permission predicate
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:16 — route gate is `requireAuth, requireAdmin, requireOrgAccess`; no `requirePermission("documents", ...)`

supabase/migrations/5302110_restore_document_permissions.sql:39-90 — `can_read_document()`: `private` requires uploader or an explicit `document_permissions.can_view` row; `internal` requires manage/admin/technician
supabase/migrations/5302110_restore_document_permissions.sql:99-107 — `documents_select_visibility_aligned` enforces `can_read_document(id)` for authenticated reads
apps/api/src/routes/documents.ts:207 — the documents list uses `getScopedClient(req, "documents", "read")`, i.e. it can enforce visibility via RLS; search cannot
findings.impact: Any tenant `admin` (even without `documents:manage` or an explicit per-document grant) can discover the names, MIME types and visibility of private/internal documents in their org by searching, bypassing the visibility model enforced everywhere else. This is exactly the 'private sensitive data must not remain searchable' control gap.
findings.recommendation: Restrict the admin-search documents query to documents the caller may read (e.g. add a `can_read_document`-equivalent predicate or an RPC, or require `documents:manage` and still filter `private`), and add a regression test asserting a private document is not returned to a non-granted admin.
findings.note: newly identified at 8d299b8d (not filed in the previous register); applies to the admin route only — portal search does not search documents. Severity could rise to P1 if private documents routinely hold HR/contract data; product/security should confirm the intended visibility of search results.

findings.title: Search router bypasses the org-pinned admin check, so a tenant admin can read another tenant's search results
evidence: apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:16 — `router.use(requireAuth, requireAdmin, requireOrgAccess)` (admin gate runs before the org scope is resolved)
apps/api/src/middleware/admin.ts:46-58 — the org pin only fires when `req.orgScope?.explicit === true && req.orgId`, i.e. after an upstream `requireOrgAccess`

apps/api/src/middleware/org-access.ts:43-60 — a cross-tenant role key (`admin`/`super_admin`, lib/roles.ts:27) in ANY approved membership grants access to any requested org and logs an impersonation event
apps/api/src/routes/audit.ts:22 — comparison routers use `requireAuth, requireOrgAccess, requireAdmin`, so the pin does apply there and the same request is 403
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:55-57,77-79 — search's own comment claims a plain tenant `admin` is scoped to their own orgs, and the route honors `req.orgScope.orgId` when `explicit`
apps/api/src/__tests__/search-tenant-scope.test.ts:71-77 — tests stub `requireOrgAccess`, so the cross-tenant grant path is never exercised
findings.impact: A tenant admin of Org A can call `GET /api/v1/search?q=...&organization_id=<Org B>` and receive Org B's tickets, projects, documents and user names/titles, while the equivalent audit/bulk routes deny the same pattern. The access is impersonation-audited, but it contradicts search's stated per-tenant scoping and ADMIN-P1-001's pin semantics.
findings.recommendation: Decide the trust model and make it consistent: either mount `requireOrgAccess` before `requireAdmin` on /search (or replicate the pin inside the handler) so a non-super admin cannot widen scope, or explicitly document `admin` as a cross-tenant MSP role and align audit/bulk. Add an integration test for tenant-admin + foreign organization_id.
findings.note: newly identified at 8d299b8d; requires an owner decision because lib/roles.ts classifies `admin` as cross-tenant while middleware/admin.ts pins it as per-tenant. The recent ?limit/counts change did not alter this path.

findings.title: Search SDK and OpenAPI contracts do not cover the implemented response (documents, counts, limit)
evidence: packages/sdk/src/search.ts:4-9 — admin `SearchResult` has no `documents`, `counts` or `limit` fields
packages/sdk/src/search.ts:20-21 — `admin(query)` sends no `limit` argument
apps/api/src/routes/search.ts:215-231 — the implemented admin response includes `documents`, `counts` and `limit`
apps/api/src/openapi/spec.ts:976-987 — both search routes document only the `q` query parameter
packages/sdk/src/__tests__/sdk-expanded.test.ts:826-833 — SDK tests mock the old shapes, so drift is not detected
findings.impact: SDK consumers cannot type or consume the documents/counts/limit the API now returns, and OpenAPI consumers cannot discover `?limit`; the contract test surface does not catch either drift.
findings.recommendation: Update the SDK types and `admin(query, options?)`, add `queryParam("limit")` to the OpenAPI search routes, and add a contract test comparing the SDK/OpenAPI shape with the route response.
findings.note: newly identified at 8d299b8d; overlaps SEARCH-P2-002 (portal `documents` declaration) but covers the admin-side SDK/OpenAPI drift introduced by the pagination change.

# Search, Indexing, and Privacy Audit

## Audit Metadata

- Audit name: repo-deep-dive
- Run: `mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8`
- Repository: `MaineCyberTech/mainecybertech` (portal monorepo, target worktree `/tmp/opencode/mct-audit-target`)
- Branch: `main` (detached at `HEAD`)
- Commit SHA: `8d299b8dc271c410b9ae2ceeda3d2c6c997af8fd` (`8d299b8d`)
- Generated at: 2026-10-11
- Auditor: subagent, prompt 31
- Area code: SEARCH
- Output path: `docs/audits/repo-deep-dive/mainecybertech-20261011-0426-full-main-8d299b8/31_search_indexing_privacy_audit.md`
- Scope limitations:

## Executive Summary

Search is a Postgres-native, real-time implementation: two authenticated REST endpoints (`GET /api/v1/search`, `GET /api/v1/search/portal`) issue `ilike`/`.or()` filters against Supabase, accelerated by GIN trigram indexes. There is no external index, indexing job, reindexing scheduler, `tsvector` column, or dedicated autocomplete endpoint, so stale-index and index-deletion problems do not exist by construction; the privacy questions are what is queried, returned, logged, and retained.

Strengths verified at this commit:

1. The sanitizer now strips every PostgREST grammar token (`.`, `,`, `()`, quotes, `\`, `%`, `*`) and caps length at 100 with regression tests (`lib/search.ts:22-33`, `sanitize-search.test.ts:32-64`).
2. Admin search scopes organizations to the caller's orgs, gates `email`/`phone` to a true platform admin, fails closed on an empty scope, and audits the all-tenants path (`search.ts:38-99,153-163`; tests `search.test.ts:173-203`, `search-tenant-scope.test.ts:136-225`).
3. Search terms are no longer persisted in plaintext: only a truncated SHA-256 fingerprint and length reach `audit_logs` (`search.ts:191-211`).
4. Admin search gained `?limit` (default 5, cap 25) and per-entity exact counts (`search.ts:28,103-155,222-231`), and the search counter is now incremented (`search.ts:213`).
5. Soft-delete columns were dropped, so deleted rows cannot silently become searchable later (`5302432`).

Material gaps at this commit:

1. **Private documents remain searchable** — the admin documents query filters only by organization and runs on the service-role client, so any tenant `admin` can discover `private`/`internal` document names that `can_read_document` would hide elsewhere. New finding.
2. **Cross-tenant search via explicit org** — because `requireAdmin` runs before `requireOrgAccess`, the org-pin never applies; a tenant admin can request another tenant's `organization_id` and read its search results (impersonation-audited), while `audit`/`bulk` deny the same pattern. New finding.
3. **Pagination fix is API-only** — portal search, both UIs, the SDK, and OpenAPI still assume 5 results with no counts; the `count: 'exact'` cost was not measured.
4. **Portal search remains the weakest surface** — no documents (SDK/doc contract still promises them), no metric, no audit, hard `.limit(5)`.
5. **Docs and contracts are stale** — module docs still say "across all organizations", attribute the portal route to the wrong file, and mark the search metric dead.

Recommended next actions: (a) filter admin-search documents by the visibility model; (b) align the search router's middleware order with `audit.ts` or document `admin` as cross-tenant; (c) finish the pagination rollout (portal + UI + SDK/OpenAPI); (d) add indexes for `organizations.slug` and `documents.name`; (e) refresh the search docs. None of the new items is a P0.

### Item: Admin global search (`GET /api/v1/search`)

### Item: Portal search (`GET /api/v1/search/portal`)

- Evidence: `search-portal.ts:9-59`; tests `search-portal.test.ts:51-115`.
- What it does: membership-derived org filter over tickets/projects; hard `.limit(5)`; no counts; no audit/metric.
- Current controls: `requireAuth`; app-level `.in("organization_id", orgIds)`; empty membership short-circuits.
- Missing controls: documents, pagination, audit/metric, RLS by default (`getScopedClient` falls back to service role unless `search-portal` is allow-listed; bypass is now recorded via `recordRlsBypass`).

### Item: Query sanitizer

- Evidence: `lib/search.ts:22-33`; tests `sanitize-search.test.ts:3-69`.
- What it does: replaces `,()."\%*` with spaces, collapses whitespace, caps 100 chars; dots are intentionally unsearchable.
- Controls: unit-tested injection strings; used by search, search-portal, knowledge-base, edu-automation.
- Residual: other list routes (`assets`, `proposals`, `findings`, …) use raw `.ilike()` values without the sanitizer; those values are passed as method arguments (not interpolated into `.or()`), so no grammar injection, but `%`/`_` wildcards pass through and results are still org-scoped.

- Evidence: `5302102:10-16`; `search.ts:29-30,140,156`.
- Gap: no index for `organizations.slug` or `documents.name`/`mime_type`; prefix columns use trigram; no `tsvector`; `count: 'exact'` on five parallel queries adds cost.

## Findings

Titles only; IDs/areas are assigned by the aggregator. Full evidence and status live in `_domains/31_search_indexing_privacy_audit.json`.

Verification rows (re-checked at 8d299b8d):

- `sanitizeSearchTerm` does not strip PostgREST `.` operator separators — **verified-fixed**.
- Admin global search exposes profile PII and never tenant-scopes the organizations query — **verified-fixed** (residual: email predicate remains for non-super callers).
- Raw search terms persisted in plaintext `audit_logs.metadata` — **verified-fixed**.
- Portal search omits documents despite SDK and documentation contract — **still-open**.
- Admin search UI silently discards the documents result set — **still-open**.
- No search pagination or result counts; hard 5-result ceiling — **partially-fixed** (admin API only).
- Search query analytics metric is dead and the analytics summary RPC is missing — **partially-fixed** (admin metric wired; RPC and portal still missing).
- Prefix/wildcard mismatch: no btree on prefix columns and no full-text (`tsvector`) search — **still-open**.
- Typeahead calls full search endpoints without rate limiting or a dedicated autocomplete surface — **partially-fixed** (global limiters only).
- Soft-delete columns are defined but never used by queries or deletes — **verified-fixed** (columns dropped).
- Search module documentation is stale relative to the code — **still-open**.

New findings (open at 8d299b8d):

- Admin global search returns private/internal documents without applying the `can_read_document` visibility filter — **P2**.
- Search router bypasses the org-pinned admin check, so a tenant admin can read another tenant's search results — **P2**.
- Search SDK and OpenAPI contracts do not cover the implemented response (documents, counts, limit) — **P3**.
